The political positions of [[Mitt Romney]] have been recorded from his [[United States Senate election in Massachusetts, 1994|1994 U.S. senatorial campaign in Massachusetts]], the [[Massachusetts gubernatorial election, 2002|2002 gubernatorial election]], during [[Governorship of Mitt Romney|his 2003–2007 governorship]], during [[Mitt Romney presidential campaign, 2008|his 2008 U.S. presidential campaign]], in his 2010 book ''[[No Apology: The Case for American Greatness]]'', during [[Mitt Romney presidential campaign, 2012|his 2012 U.S. presidential campaign]], and during his [[2018 United States Senate election in Utah|2018 senatorial campaign in Utah]]. Some of these political positions have changed, while others have remained unchanged.

In 1994, during his campaign for [[United States Senate elections, 1994|US Senate]] in Massachusetts, "Romney has cast himself as a [[moderate Republican (modern United States)|moderate Republican]], socially liberal and fiscally conservative" and ''[[The New York Times]]'' likened his views to those of Governor [[Bill Weld|William F. Weld]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1994/10/25/us/the-1994-campaign-massachusetts-perfect-anti-kennedy-opposes-the-senator.html|title=THE 1994 CAMPAIGN: MASSACHUSETTS; 'Perfect Anti-Kennedy' Opposes the Senator|last=and|first=Sara Rimer|work=The New York Times |date=25 October 1994 |access-date=2018-08-06|language=en}}</ref> During his [[Massachusetts gubernatorial election, 2002|gubernatorial campaign]] in 2002, Romney described himself as a [[Centrism|centrist]] saying of himself: "I'm someone who is moderate, and ... my views are progressive."<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/romney-in-2002-called-his-views-progressive/|title=Romney in 2002 called his views "progressive"|access-date=2018-08-06|language=en}}</ref> ''[[The Boston Globe]]'', reporting on the 2004 Republican National Convention list of speakers, wrote that "Massachusetts Republicans with moderate positions on most social issues, Romney and [Lt. ==Economic policy==
===Agriculture===
In his 1994 Senate campaign, Romney called for the "virtual elimination" of the federal [[United States Department of Agriculture|Department of Agriculture]]<ref>{{Cite news |last=Burns |first=Douglas |title=Romney Once Called For Cutting Farm Subsidies, 'Virtual' Elimination Of USDA |newspaper=The Iowa Independent |publisher=American Independent News Network |date=June 26, 2007 |url=http://iowaindependent.com/?s=433&key=old_id |access-date=2011-02-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713052525/http://iowaindependent.com/?s=433&key=old_id |archive-date=2011-07-13 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and for reductions in farm subsidies.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Romney's positions in 1994 |newspaper=[[The Boston Globe]] |date=March 19, 2002 |url=https://www.boston.com/news/daily/romney_positions.htm |access-date=2011-02-20 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080513111632/http://www.boston.com/news/daily/romney_positions.htm |archive-date=May 13, 2008 }}</ref>  In 2007, when questioned about these views, a Romney for President Iowa campaign spokesman responded: "Governor Romney believes that investing in agriculture is key to our economy and families."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Burns |first=Douglas |title=Romney Responds to Iowa Independent Story On Farm Subsidy Comments |newspaper=The Iowa Independent |publisher=American Independent News Network |date=June 27, 2007 |url=http://iowaindependent.com/441/romney-responds-to-iowa-independent-story-on-farm-subsidy-comments# |access-date=2011-02-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713052532/http://iowaindependent.com/441/romney-responds-to-iowa-independent-story-on-farm-subsidy-comments |archive-date=2011-07-13 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

During the 2012 presidential election campaign, Romney took positions on [[agricultural subsidy|agricultural subsidies]] that some media reports characterized as vague and somewhat contradictory.<ref name=harvest>{{cite news|last=Bernfeld|first=Jeremy|title=Republicans on the farm|url=http://harvestpublicmedia.org/article/924/republicans-farm/5#Romney|newspaper=Harvest Public Media|date=December 15, 2011|access-date=2012-09-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120926175614/http://harvestpublicmedia.org/article/924/republicans-farm/5#Romney|archive-date=2012-09-26|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Weyl|first=Ben|title=Energy and Iowa: the declining power of ethanol|url=http://www.rollcall.com/features/Outlook_Swing-States/outlook/-210712-1.html|newspaper=Roll Call|date=December 1, 2011}}</ref><ref name=goodtimes>{{cite news|last=Hicks|first=Lynn|title=Farmers' agenda: keep goodtimes rolling|url=http://caucuses.desmoinesregister.com/2011/12/18/farmers-agenda-keep-good-times-rolling/|newspaper=Des Moines Register|date=December 18, 2011}}</ref> In May 2011, just days after rival Republican presidential candidate [[Tim Pawlenty]] had declared that federal subsidies for the production of [[ethanol fuel]] should be phased out, Romney said that he was a supporter of ethanol subsidies.<ref>Jonathan Weisman. [https://blogs.wsj.com/washwire/2011/05/27/romney-hearts-ethanol-subsidies/?mod=WSJBlog "Romney Hearts Ethanol Subsidies"], Washington Wire (blog), ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' (May 27, 2011).</ref> Five months later, while speaking on agricultural subsidies at a roundtable discussion with Iowa farmers and business leaders, Romney said, "I'm not running for office based on making promises of handing out money. ... We're going to have to live within our means."<ref name=leyssubs>{{cite news|last=Leys|first=Tony|title=Romney declines to commit to specific farm supports|url=http://caucuses.desmoinesregister.com/2011/10/20/romney-declines-to-commit-to-specific-farm-supports/|newspaper=Des Moines Register|date=October 20, 2011|access-date=September 28, 2012|archive-date=April 26, 2012|archive-url=https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20120426202119/http://caucuses.desmoinesregister.com/2011/10/20/romney-declines-to-commit-to-specific-farm-supports/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He also said that while he had supported ethanol subsidies in the past in order to help the ethanol fuel industry become established, and that he continued to believe that ethanol should play a role in meeting the nation's energy needs, he agreed with the discontinuation of the tax credit for production of ethanol from corn that was scheduled to occur two months later.<ref name=leyssubs/> On the subject of agricultural subsidies more generally, Romney wrote in response to a 2012 questionnaire from the [[American Farm Bureau Federation]] that "other nations subsidize their farmers, so we must be careful not to unilaterally change our policies in a way that would disadvantage agriculture here in our country."<ref name=farmbureau>{{cite web|title=Decision 2012: American Farm Bureau Federation Questionnaire for Presidential Candidates|url=http://www.fb.org/index.php?action=legislative.2012presidentialQuestionnaire|publisher=American Farm Bureau Federation|access-date=September 27, 2012|archive-date=November 14, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121114181002/http://www.fb.org/index.php?action=legislative.2012presidentialQuestionnaire|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made similar remarks on the campaign trail in August 2012, without explicitly referring to subsidies: "We don't want to find ourselves with regards to our food supply in the same kind of position we are in with our energy supply, so it's important for us to make sure that our farmers are able to stay on the farm and raise the crops that we need to have a secure source of food. So I believe in supports that will allow us to do that."<ref>{{cite news|last=Wyant|first=Sara|title=Obama's farm bill proposals compared to Romney's approach|url=http://articles.orlandosentinel.com/2012-08-24/news/aan-ff.08-24-12.agripulse-20120824_1_farm-bill-programs-that-benefit-farmers-farm-safety/2|newspaper=Orlando Sentinel|date=August 24, 2012|access-date=2012-09-28|archive-date=2015-04-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402223635/http://articles.orlandosentinel.com/2012-08-24/news/aan-ff.08-24-12.agripulse-20120824_1_farm-bill-programs-that-benefit-farmers-farm-safety/2|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Romney's position on federal mandates that require gasoline producers to include ethanol in gasoline blends has been less clear.<ref name=goodtimes/> The Romney campaign responded to a survey question asking for Romney's position on ethanol use mandates by saying the ethanol industry "has made important strides in reducing America's dependence on foreign oil" and ethanol "should continue to have prospects for growing its share in transportation fuels."<ref name=goodtimes/> Romney wrote to the American Farm Bureau Federation, "The increased production of biofuels plays an important part in my plan to achieve energy independence. In order to support increased market penetration and competition among energy sources, I am in favor of maintaining the Renewable Fuel Standard."<ref name=farmbureau/>

Romney declined to respond to survey questions from the Iowa Corn Growers Association requesting his positions on crop insurance and conservation during the presidential primary campaign.<ref name=harvest/> He responded to an American Farm Bureau Federation questionnaire in 2012 by saying, "my immediate priority [as president] should be given to enacting disaster relief for those not traditionally covered by crop insurance as this year's drought has worsened."<ref name=farmbureau/>

During the 2008 presidential primary campaign, Romney had distinguished his prescription for the automotive industry from rival candidate [[John McCain]]'s by calling for a five-fold increase, to $20 billion per year over five years, in federal funding for research and development in energy, fuel technology, materials science, and automotive technology. In a January 14 speech, he stated, "I'm not willing to sit back and say, ' ... Too bad for the people who've lost their jobs. They're gone forever.'"<ref name=DAG1>David A. Graham. [https://www.theatlantic.com/politics/archive/2012/04/a-short-history-of-mitt-romneys-views-on-the-detroit-bailout/256513/ "A Short History of Mitt Romney's Views on the Detroit Bailout"], ''[[The Atlantic]]'' (April 30, 2012).</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Luo|first=Michael|title=Romney battles McCain for Michigan lead|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/01/14/us/politics/14web-repubs.html|newspaper=The New York Times|date=January 14, 2008}}</ref> As the [[2008–2010 automotive industry crisis]] arose during the [[2008 financial crisis]] and the [[Great Recession]], Romney argued against a bailout with direct government loans of the auto industry. ===Campaign finance===
In his 1994 Senate campaign, Romney advocated spending limits on congressional campaigns and suggested abolishing [[political action committee]]s.<ref name="Campaign-finance"/>
In his 2002 gubernatorial campaign, Romney proposed taxing private political contributions in order to finance publicly funded campaigns.<ref name="Campaign-finance"/>
In 2007 Romney began criticizing the [[McCain-Feingold Law]], saying "We step into dangerous territory when politicians start eviscerating our fundamental freedoms in the name of amorphous principles, like campaign finance reform."<ref name="Campaign-finance">{{cite news|url=http://thehill.com/leading-the-news/romneys-about-face-on-campaign-funding-2007-02-08.html|title=Romney's about face on campaign funding|last=Bolton|first=Alexander|work=The Hill|date=2007-02-08|access-date=2007-03-15|archive-date=2007-11-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071118085947/http://thehill.com/leading-the-news/romneys-about-face-on-campaign-funding-2007-02-08.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
He wrote in 2007: "The original intent of McCain-Feingold was to reduce the role of money and special interests in our political system. But on this too it has been a failure. Political spending has been driven into secret corners and more power and influence has been handed to hidden special interests. What is really needed is greater transparency, and disclosure, of campaign contributions – not more restrictions on political speech."<ref>Romney, Mitt. [http://townhall.com/columnists/mittromney/2007/04/25/the_fundamental_flaws_in_the_mccain-feingold_law/page/full/ "The Fundamental Flaws in the McCain-Feingold Law."] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306195000/http://townhall.com/columnists/mittromney/2007/04/25/the_fundamental_flaws_in_the_mccain-feingold_law/page/full |date=2016-03-06 }} ''Mitt Romney'', 25 April 2007.</ref>

In November 2011, Romney said that the [[Supreme Court of the United States|Supreme Court]] had made the right decision in its 2010 ''[[Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission]]'' ruling, but that he did not like some of the consequences of it: "I'm not wild about the idea of corporations making political contributions as a concept. I think their decision was a correct decision. I support their decision. I wish we could find a way to get money out of politics. I haven't found a way to do that."<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.ibtimes.com/articles/243651/20111104/romney-backs-citizens-united-ruling-wild-corporate.htm | title=Romney Backs Citizens United, But 'Not Wild' About Corporate Campaign Spending  | author=Rivoli, Dan | newspaper=[[International Business Times]] | date=November 4, 2011}}</ref>  In January 2012, in the midst of the Republican Party presidential nomination primaries battle, Romney criticized the existence of [[Super PAC]]s that were playing a large role in the campaign, saying, "I'll tell you, there have been some—there have been some attacks on me that have just been outrageous and completely inaccurate and have been shown to be inaccurate. That's the nature of the process. I hope it ends. ... We all would like to have super PACs disappear, to tell you the truth ... I think this has to change."<ref name="camp-beast">{{cite news | url=http://www.thedailybeast.com/articles/2012/01/17/mitt-romney-newt-gingrich-lament-super-pacs-but-backed-ruling-that-made-them.html | title=Mitt Romney, Newt Gingrich Lament Super PACs but Backed Ruling That Made Them | author=Stone, Daniel | newspaper=[[The Daily Beast]] | date=January 17, 2012}}</ref>  A Romney spokesman added at the time that Romney viewed laws limiting regular donations to candidates' campaigns as too restrictive, which resulted in money going to Super PACs instead, and that it would be better if candidates' campaigns could receive those monies directly and take responsibility for ads made with them.<ref name="camp-beast"/>

===Deficit===
Romney (like several other Republican candidates) signed the "cut, cap and balance" pledge, under which an increase in the federal [[debt ceiling]] would be contingent on major cuts in spending, caps on spending, and a [[Balanced Budget Amendment|balanced-budget amendment]] to the [[United States Constitution|Constitution]].<ref>{{Citation | last = Sonmez| first = Felicia| title = Romney supports 'cut, cap, balance' pledge| newspaper = [[The Washington Post]]| date = June 29, 2011| url = https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/2chambers/post/romney-supports-cut-cap-balance-pledge/2011/06/29/AGbXD4qH_blog.html| access-date = 2011-07-03}}</ref>

Romney opposed the [[Budget Control Act of 2011]] that was passed to resolve the [[United States debt-ceiling crisis of 2011|United States debt-ceiling crisis]] as part of a deal struck between President Obama and congressional leaders, including his future running mate, Paul Ryan.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mitt Romney Issues Statement on Debt Ceiling Deal|url=http://mittromney.com/press/2011/08/mitt-romney-statement-debt-ceiling-deal|publisher=Mitt Romney For President|access-date=1 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111001202512/http://mittromney.com/press/2011/08/mitt-romney-statement-debt-ceiling-deal|archive-date=2011-10-01|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>[https://www.cbsnews.com/video/watch/?id=7421090n "Ryan: Why I voted for sequestration."] ''CBS News'', 9 September 2012.</ref> Romney later criticized Obama for failing to specify the true impact of the resulting sequestration, as required by law.<ref>Wasson, Erik. [https://thehill.com/video/campaign/248307-romney-criticizes-gop-leaders-over-debt-ceiling-deal-/ "Romney: GOP leaders made ‘big mistake’ agreeing to sequester."]  ''The Hill'', 8 September 2012.</ref>

===Energy and the environment===

====During Massachusetts governorship====
{{see also|Governorship of Mitt Romney#Environment}}
Romney's positions on energy policy and environmental protection regulations shifted from his time as governor of Massachusetts to his campaign for the presidency in the 2012 election.<ref name=keithenergy>{{cite news|last=Keith|first=Tamara|title=On energy policy, Romney's emphasis has shifted|url=https://www.npr.org/2012/04/02/149812295/on-energy-policy-another-shift-for-romney|publisher=NPR|date=April 2, 2012}}</ref><ref name=nytnrgs>{{cite news|last=Stolberg|first=Sheryl Gay|title=Romney shifted right on energy as presidential politics beckoned|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/09/30/us/politics/romney-energy-agenda-shifted.html?pagewanted=all|newspaper=The New York Times|date=September 29, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Pexton|first=Patrick B.|title=Mitt Romney's energy evolution: Did The Post mislead readers?|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/mitt-romneys-energy-evolution-did-the-post-mislead-readers/2012/06/22/gJQAS6R3vV_story.html|newspaper=The Washington Post|date=June 22, 2012}}</ref><ref name=kuci0911>{{cite news|last=Kucinich|first=Jackie|title=Romney's record differs from record as governor|url=https://www.usatoday.com/news/washington/story/2011-09-07/Romneys-energy-rhetoric-differs-from-his-record-as-governor/50304822/1|newspaper=USA Today|date=September 8, 2011}}</ref>

As a candidate for governor of Massachusetts in 2002,<ref name=mon2002>{{cite news|last=Monahan|first=John J.|title=Candidates frustrate environmentalists|newspaper=Worcester Telegram & Gazette|date=October 29, 2002}}</ref> and later as governor,<ref name=monahan2004>{{cite news|last=Monahan|first=John J.|title=Romney unveils plan to cut air pollution - Environment, energy costs are targeted|newspaper=Worcester Telegram & Gazette|date=May 7, 2004}}</ref> Romney prioritized policies that would promote energy conservation and reduce environmental pollution. He said that he was "absolutely committed" to renewable energy and that "I think the global warming debate is now pretty much over and people recognize the need associated with providing sources which do not generate the heat currently provided by fossil fuels."<ref name=windpower>{{cite news|last=Coleman|first=Jack|title=Wind power gets boost, but Cape plan shunned|newspaper=Cape Cod Times|date=March 14, 2003}}</ref>

Campaigning for the governorship, he argued in support of measures such as imposing higher taxes on [[SUV]]s to help reduce auto emissions and conserve energy; revitalizing urban neighborhoods using fees charged to developers for cutting down trees in suburban areas; and doubling the rate of cleanup of [[brownfield land]]s.<ref name=mon2002/>

In his first 100 days in office as governor, he proposed expansion of the beverage container deposit law ([[bottle bill]]), a switch by state government agencies to the use of environmentally friendly cleansers, and clean up of the state's "Filthy Five" power plants.<ref name=nissman>{{cite news|last=Nissman|first=Cara|title=Not easy being green: As Earth Day nears, groups hope to rejuvenate environmental agenda|newspaper=The Boston Herald|date=April 20, 2003}}</ref> He appointed a prominent environmentalist, [[Douglas I. Foy|Douglas Foy]], to oversee energy development, transportation, housing, and environmental affairs.<ref name=nissman /> Foy helped develop an energy and environment plan that included 72 public and private initiatives, with a goal of deriving 15 percent of the state's electricity from [[renewable energy|renewable sources]] such as wind, solar, and nonpolluting [[fuel cells]] by 2020, and of reducing [[greenhouse gas emissions]] of state agencies by 25 percent. The plan also proposed to impose strict [[emissions standards]] on older power plants and sought to substantially reduce soot emissions from diesel buses, trucks, and heavy construction equipment.<ref name=monahan2004 />

Arguing for environmental protection regulations in 2003, Romney said that "if the choice is between dirty power plants or protecting the health of the people of Massachusetts, I will always come down on the side of public health."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sierraclub.org/planet/200302/clean_air_act.asp |title=Bush Chips Away at Clean Air Act |date=March 2003 |first=Tom |last=Valtin |work=Planet Newsletter |publisher=Sierra Club |access-date=January 15, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111029215307/http://www.sierraclub.org/planet/200302/clean_air_act.asp |archive-date=October 29, 2011 }}</ref> He insisted that a coal power plant not delay in meeting tough emissions standards even at the cost of losing jobs: "I will not create jobs or hold jobs that kill people. ... And that plant, that plant kills people."<ref name=nytnrgs/>

As governor, he also argued for limits on oil and gas drilling in order to protect the environment. In his state of the Commonwealth address in January 2005, Romney said, "I'm concerned about the preservation of our natural resources. I will file legislation to protect our oceans from off shore drilling and commercial development. The oceans should not be up for grabs like some Wild West land rush."<ref>{{cite news|last=Kibbe|first=David|title=School reform plan offered|newspaper=Cape Cod Times|date=January 14, 2005}}</ref> He signed into law a bill to protect against oil spills and to increase penalties for polluters.<ref name=nytnrgs/><ref>{{cite news|title=Oil tankers face stricter standards|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-7863011.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160307214355/https://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-7863011.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 7, 2016|newspaper=The Boston Globe|date=August 5, 2004}}</ref>

He pursued policies to make greater use of carpooling and public transit, and sought tax credits to stimulate purchases of [[Hybrid electric vehicle|hybrid]] and other more fuel-efficient vehicles.<ref name=tnr1019646>{{Cite web|url=https://newrepublic.com/article/101946/mitt-romney-massachusetts-governor-gas-prices-renewable-energy|title=When Romney Liked High Gas Prices|via=The New Republic}}</ref><ref>http://www.massclimateaction.org/pdf/MAClimateProtPlan0504.pdfM{{dead link|date=March 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Romney argued that tax policy should be used to promote energy conservation. When his lieutenant governor supported a temporary suspension of the state gasoline tax to provide consumers some relief during a period of especially high gasoline prices in 2006, Romney rejected the proposal, arguing that maintaining the tax would help encourage energy conservation: "I don't think that now is the time, and I'm not sure there will be the right time, for us to encourage the use of more gasoline. ... I am very much in favor of people recognizing that these high gasoline prices are probably here to stay and that the appropriate action for us to take is to find ways to find fuel conservation."<ref name=leblancgastax>{{cite news|last=LeBlanc|first=Steve|title=Healey, Romney at odds on gas tax rollback|newspaper=The Boston Globe|date=May 3, 2006}}</ref>

He highlighted support for government investment in developing sources of renewable energy, such as wind and solar, early in his administration,<ref name=kuci0911 /><ref>{{cite news|last=Coleman|first=Jack|title=Governor's energy figures don't add up|newspaper=Cape Cod Times|date=March 17, 2003}}</ref> although he opposed a proposal that would have sited a [[wind farm]] in Nantucket Sound off Cape Cod, where he said the visual impact would be detrimental to the state's tourist economy.<ref name=windpower />

Romney initially supported a [[Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative|regional greenhouse gas cap-and-trade initiative]] for New England and eastern Canada,<ref>{{cite news|last=Helman|first=Scott|title=Romney favors pact by states on emissions|url=https://www.boston.com/news/local/articles/2005/11/08/romney_favors_pact_by_states_on_emissions/|newspaper=The Boston Globe|date=November 8, 2005}}</ref> but he ultimately withdrew his support when he was unable to ensure establishment of certain limits on the penalty fees businesses would be charged for exceeding emissions allowances.<ref name="bg-rggi-out">{{cite news |url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-7928566.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150130000323/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-7928566.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 30, 2015|title=Mass. Pulls Out of Agreement to Cut Power Plant Emissions|first=Beth|last=Daley|newspaper=The Boston Globe|date=December 15, 2005}}{{subscription required}}</ref> A week later, his administration issued a rule allowing companies to pay a fine instead of having to clean up emissions of toxins like mercury.<ref name=banenergy>{{cite news|last=Banerkee|first=Neela|title=Mitt Romney worked to combat climate change as governor|url=https://www.latimes.com/la-xpm-2012-jun-13-la-na-romney-energy-20120613-story.html|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|date=June 13, 2012}}</ref> Both decisions were made as Romney announced he would not run for a second term as governor and began to focus on entering the 2008 presidential campaign.<ref name=banenergy/> Some former Romney policy advisors later told ''The New York Times'' that his political team had been afraid that, with industry being opposed to the cap-and-trade proposal, Romney's having included Massachusetts in the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative would have made Romney's chance of winning a presidential campaign very unlikely.<ref name=nytnrgs/>

===Disaster relief===

As governor of Massachusetts, Romney requested federal disaster assistance to help with cleaning up after storms.<ref name=wapofema>{{cite news|last=O'Keefe|first=Ed|title=Hurricane Sandy highlights how Obama and Romney respond to disasters|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/decision2012/hurricane-sandy-highlights-how-obama-and-romney-respond-to-disasters/2012/10/29/85ae66a2-21db-11e2-ac85-e669876c6a24_story.html|newspaper=The Washington Post|date=October 29, 2012}}</ref>

During the 2012 presidential primary campaign, when asked what the federal government's role should be in responding to natural disasters, Romney suggested that responsibility for handling disasters should be taken from [[Federal Emergency Management Agency|FEMA]], the federal agency dedicated to disaster relief, and given to the states, or outsourced to the private sector: "Every time you have an occasion to take something from the federal government and send it back to the states, that's the right direction. And if you can go even further, and send it back to the private sector, that's even better. Instead of thinking in the federal budget, what we should cut -- we should ask ourselves the opposite question. What should we keep? We should take all of what we're doing at the federal level and say, what are the things we're doing that we don't have to do? And those things we've got to stop doing, because we're borrowing $1.6 trillion more this year than we're taking in."<ref name=phillyfema>{{cite news|last1=Pace|first1=Julie|last2=Peoples|first2=Steve|title=Storm in spotlight in campaign's final full week|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/news/politics/presidential/20121029_ap_storminspotlightincampaignsfinalfullweek.html|newspaper=Philadelphia Inquirer|date=October 29, 2012}}</ref><ref name=CNNdebatefema>{{cite news|title=CNN Presidential primary debate Manchester, New Hampshire (transcript)|url=http://transcripts.cnn.com/TRANSCRIPTS/1106/13/se.02.html|work=CNN|date=June 13, 2011}}</ref> Asked whether by that he specifically meant disaster relief, he replied, "we cannot afford to do those things without jeopardizing the future for our kids. It is simply immoral, in my view, for us to continue to rack up larger and larger debts and pass them on to our kids, knowing full well that we'll all be dead and gone before it's paid off. It makes no sense at all."<ref name=CNNdebatefema/>

The Romney campaign told reporters in October 2012, as the nation's East coast braced for [[Hurricane Sandy]], that "Gov. Romney believes that states should be in charge of emergency management in responding to storms and other natural disasters in their jurisdictions. ... As the first responders, states are in the best position to aid affected individuals and communities and to direct resources and assistance to where they are needed most. This includes help from the federal government and FEMA."<ref name=wapofema/> The Romney campaign released a statement following the storm stating, "I believe that FEMA plays a key role in working with states and localities to prepare for and respond to natural disasters. As president, I will ensure FEMA has the funding it needs to fulfill its mission, while directing maximum resources to the first responders who work tirelessly to help those in need, because states and localities are in the best position to get aid to the individuals and communities affected by natural disasters."<ref>{{cite news|last=Taylor|first=Andrew|title=Romney faces scrutiny on aid in storm's wake|url=https://www.chron.com/news/politics/article/Romney-faces-scrutiny-on-aid-in-storm-s-wake-3995151.php|agency=Associated Press|newspaper=Houston Chronicle|date=November 1, 2012}}{{Dead link|date=July 2022 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

He said he opposed efforts to provide non-emergency health coverage to undocumented immigrants and he supported the [[Hyde Amendment]] prohibiting government funding for elective abortion.<ref name="ontheissues.org"/> Romney opposed a federal [[single-payer health care|single-payer system]], but supported state efforts to reduce the uninsured population.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.foxnews.com/story/0,2933,557283,00.html |title=Governor Bobby Jindal Discusses Health Care Reform He Wants to See - Neil Cavuto |publisher=FOXNews.com |date=2009-09-29 |access-date=2010-06-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091003000656/http://www.foxnews.com/story/0,2933,557283,00.html |archive-date=2009-10-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The Massachusetts health care law was used as an early model for Democratic health insurance reforms in 2009.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cnn.com/2009/POLITICS/08/20/romney.health.care/index.html|title='Romney care' touted as a model for national health care reform |author1=Jim Acosta |author2=Ed Hornick|website=CNN|language=en|access-date=2018-06-28}}</ref>

==== Medicare ====

While campaigning for the governorship of Massachusetts in 2002, Romney argued that the federal government should pay for medicines for seniors: "It is outrageous that some senior citizens are forced to choose between paying for their prescription drugs and their groceries. The federal government needs to step in with a plan for our senior citizens, and I will lobby officials on the federal level to provide a [[Medicare (United States)|Medicare]] drug benefit."<ref>{{cite news|title=Governor hopefuls debate|newspaper=Sunday Republican|date=October 27, 2002|location=Springfield, Massachusetts}}</ref> (The U.S. Congress would pass legislation providing for Medicare prescription drug coverage - [[Medicare Part D]] - the following year.)

In February 2012, in an address to the Detroit Economic Club during which he discussed his recently unveiled economic plan and federal budget proposal, Romney said that to help control government healthcare expenditures, as president he would seek to gradually raise the minimum age for Medicare eligibility. The change in eligibility would affect future Medicare beneficiaries who at the time of enactment of the rule change would be 54 years of age or younger; the eligibility age would be raised by one month per year, then eventually tied to life-expectancy.<ref>{{cite news|last=Hunt|first=Kasie|title=Romney would raise Medicare eligibility age|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/feedarticle/10111733|agency=AP foreign|newspaper=The Guardian|date=February 24, 2012|location=London}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Jennings|first=Natalie|title=Mitt Romney speaks to Detroit economic club (transcript, video)|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/election-2012/post/mitt-romney-speaks-to-the-detroit-economic-club-live-video/2012/02/24/gIQAX5vxXR_blog.html|newspaper=The Washington Post|date=February 24, 2012}}</ref>

Romney named Representative [[Paul Ryan]] as his vice-presidential running mate in August 2012. A year earlier, in June 2011, the Republican-controlled U.S. House of Representatives had passed a Republican alternative budget proposed by Ryan, with no Democrats voting for it. One controversial aspect of the proposal concerned Medicare; for those under age 55 as of its enactment, it would replace the existing Medicare system in which the government pays doctors, hospitals, and other medical providers fees for services rendered with a system in which the government would instead pay vouchers (also referred to as premium-support subsidies) to Medicare beneficiaries, who could then use their vouchers to either buy private medical insurance or to obtain coverage in a plan similar to traditional Medicare.<ref name=medipolitifact>{{cite news|last=Jacobson|first=Louis|title=Do Mitt Romney and Paul Ryan want to turn Medicare into a voucher program?|url=http://www.politifact.com/truth-o-meter/statements/2012/aug/16/barack-obama/does-paul-ryan-want-turn-medicare-voucher-program/|newspaper=Politifact.com (Tampa Bay Times)|date=August 16, 2012}}</ref> Romney said that as president he would sign such a plan if it reached his desk, but he added that he would be putting forward his own plan before debating Obama.<ref name="redsox">{{cite news| last = Friedman| first = Emily| title = Romney Talks to ABC News About Health Care, Jobs, Ties and Red Sox | work = [[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]| date = June 2, 2011 | url = http://blogs.abcnews.com/thenote/2011/06/romney-talks-to-abc-news-about-health-care-jobs-ties-and-red-sox.html | access-date = 2011-06-03}}</ref>

During an interview in August 2012, several days after choosing Ryan as his running mate, Romney said, "Paul Ryan and my plan for Medicare, I think, is the same, if not identical -- it's probably close to identical."<ref name=medipolitifact/>

A 2012 study by the Kaiser Family Foundation said, in October 2012, that a hypothetical Medicare plan along the lines of Romney would raise premiums for nearly 6 out of 10 seniors.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10000872396390443675404578059014083323672|title=U.S. Watch|date=October 16, 2012|via=www.wsj.com}}</ref>  The Romney campaign noted that the study did not specifically model any proposal from either campaign.<ref>{{cite magazine|author=Rick Ungar |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/rickungar/2012/10/15/its-official-non-partisan-kaiser-foundation-says-60-of-seniors-would-pay-more-for-medicare-under-romney-ryan-voucher-plan/ |title=It's Official: Non-Partisan Kaiser Foundation Says 60% Of Seniors Would Pay More For Medicare Under Romney-Ryan Voucher Plan |magazine=Forbes |date=2012-04-18 |access-date=2012-11-07}}</ref>

===Stimulus===
As governor of Massachusetts, Romney favored the use of [[economic stimulus]] measures, using both federal funding and state funding to help lift the state's sluggish economy. Just months into his tenure as governor, in April 2003, while he shied away from any public endorsement of the tax cuts proposed by the Bush Administration, he argued for federal funds to stimulate the local economy: "I very much support an economic stimulus. ... An economic stimulus is a good thing for Massachusetts."<ref name=bushtaxcut>{{cite news|last1=Washington|first1=Wayne|last2=Johnson|first2=Glen|title=Romney weighs in - carefully - on Bush tax-cut plan: Governor won't give his endorsement|newspaper=The Boston Globe|date=April 11, 2003}}</ref> That same year, he proposed his own economic stimulus package of tax credits and grants to promote the state's high technology industry, ultimately totaling $100 million when agreed to by the legislature.<ref name=masonstim>{{cite news|last=Mason|first=Edward|title=The stimulus plan that Romney forgot|url=http://www.salon.com/2012/02/27/the_stimulus_plan_that_romney_forgot/|newspaper=Salon.com|date=February 27, 2012}}</ref> Two years later, in February 2005, he proposed a much larger stimulus package, totaling $600 million, that he said would create 20,000 jobs over 5 years. In early January 2009, Romney supported the $750 billion federal economic stimulus package proposed by the incoming president, Barack Obama, who had not yet taken office. Romney said at the time:

<blockquote>I frankly wish that the last Congress would have dealt with the stimulus issue and that the president [outgoing President George W. Bush] could assign that before leaving office. I think there is need for economic stimulus. Americans have lost about $11 trillion in net worth. That translates into about $400 billion a year less spending that they'll be doing, and that's net of additional government programs like Medicaid and unemployment insurance. And government can help make that up in a very difficult time. ... I'd move quickly. These are unusual times. But it has to be something which relieves pressure on middle-income families. I think a tax cut is necessary for them as well as for businesses that are growing. We'll be investing in infrastructure and in energy technologies.<ref>{{cite web| title = Cnn late edition with wolf blitzer| publisher = CNN| date = January 4, 2009| url = http://www-cgi.cnn.com/TRANSCRIPTS/0901/04/le.01.html| access-date = 2011-12-28| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120117020415/http://www-cgi.cnn.com/TRANSCRIPTS/0901/04/le.01.html| archive-date = 2012-01-17| url-status = dead}}</ref></blockquote>

However, as a candidate for president in May 2012, Romney said that the economic stimulus package that had been enacted in February 2009 (the [[American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009]]) had been a waste of money that did little to jump-start the economy, and that the federal government had inflated the numbers of jobs that had been created or preserved by the various projects funded through the stimulus program.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.latimes.com/la-xpm-2012-may-18-la-pn-romney-new-hampshire-bridge-stimulus-20120518-story.html | work=Los Angeles Times | first=Maeve | last=Reston | title=Mitt Romney chides stimulus spending at N.H. Romney supports sentencing under the [[three strikes law]].<ref>{{Cite news| first=Raphael | last=Lewis | title= Romney files death penalty bill |date=April 29, 2005 | url=https://www.boston.com/news/local/articles/2005/04/29/romney_files_death_penalty_bill?pg=full | work=[[The Boston Globe]] | access-date = 2007-04-20 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news| first=Maria | last=Sacchetti | title= Romney plan would greatly boost charter schools |date=February 1, 2005 | url=https://www.boston.com/news/local/articles/2005/02/01/romney_plan_would_greatly_boost_charter_schools/ | work=[[The Boston Globe]] | access-date = 2007-04-20 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news| title= Mitt Romney on crime |year= 1994 | url=http://www.ontheissues.org/Crime.htm | work=OnTheIssues | access-date = 2007-04-20 }}</ref>  Romney supports mandatory increases in sentencing for repeat drunk drivers and has supported a federal effort to curtail the drug trade in Colombia.<ref name="ontheissues.org"/>

As governor of Massachusetts, Romney sought to reinstate the state's [[Death-penalty|death penalty]],<ref name=deathpenalty>{{cite news | author = Lewis, Raphael | url = https://www.boston.com/news/local/articles/2005/04/29/romney_files_death_penalty_bill/ | title = Romney files death penalty bill, Measure sets out tight restriction | work = [[The Boston Globe]] | date = April 29, 2005 }}
</ref> which had been ruled unconstitutional by the state Supreme Judicial Court in 1982.<ref>{{cite news|last=Quinn|first=Garrett|title=The complicated history of the death penalty in Massachusetts, from the Salem witch trials to Dzhokhar Tsarnaev|url=http://www.masslive.com/news/boston/index.ssf/2014/02/history_of_the_death_penalty_i.html|newspaper=The Republican|date=February 11, 2014}}</ref> The legislation Romney proposed would have called for the [[Death-penalty|death penalty]] in cases that included terrorism, the assassination of law enforcement officials, murders involving prolonged torture, or multiple killings. Under the proposed legislation, for a death sentence to be rendered there would have had to be scientific evidence of the defendant's guilt, such as evidence based on [[DNA profiling|DNA analysis]]; and the tougher standard of "no doubt" of guilt (as opposed to the standard of proof "beyond a reasonable doubt" that is traditionally employed in criminal cases) would also have had to be met. The legislation called for a pool of certified capital case lawyers to ensure proper representation for the accused, and would have allowed citizens who do not personally support the death penalty to still serve as jurors in the pre-sentencing phase of trials, during which decisions are made on the defendants' guilt.<ref name="deathpenalty"/> The bill was defeated in the Massachusetts House of Representatives by a vote of 100–53.<ref>[https://www.boston.com/news/local/articles/2005/11/16/death_penalty_bill_fails_in_house/ Death penalty bill fails in house] Boston.com, Nov. 16, 2005</ref>

===Evolution===
As Governor of Massachusetts, Romney supported the teaching of [[evolution]], and opposed the teaching of [[intelligent design]], in public school science classes, stating so in December 2005 during his term,<ref name="bg-evo">{{cite news | url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-7932901.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130502181313/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-7932901.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=May 2, 2013 | title=Romney says media distort his views | author=Phillips, Frank | newspaper=The Boston Globe | date=December 22, 2005}}{{subscription required}}</ref> and then in May 2007 – shortly after his term concluded – saying, "In my opinion, the science class is where to teach evolution, or if there are other scientific thoughts that need to be discussed. If we're going to talk about more philosophical matters, like why it was created, and was there an intelligent designer behind it, that's for the religion class or philosophy class or social studies class."<ref name="nyt-evo">{{cite news | url=http://thecaucus.blogs.nytimes.com/2007/05/11/romney-elaborates-on-evolution/ | title=Romney Elaborates on Evolution | author=Luo, Michael | newspaper=The New York Times | date=May 11, 2007}}</ref>  Romney expressed his own views in May 2007 by saying, "I believe that God designed the universe and created the universe. And I believe evolution is most likely the process he used to create the human body. ... I'm not exactly sure what is meant by intelligent design. But I believe God is intelligent and I believe he designed the creation. And I believe he used the process of evolution to create the human body."<ref name="nyt-evo"/>  He said that when faculty members interviewing him for an honors designation asked for his beliefs on the subject before his 1971 graduation from [[Brigham Young University]], he told them that there was "[no conflict] between true science and true religion".<ref name="nyt-evo"/>  At a [[Republican Party presidential debates, 2008#May 3, 2007 - Simi Valley, California|May 2007 Republican Party presidential debate]], Romney was not one of several candidates that raised their hands to indicate they did not accept evolution.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/05/03/us/politics/04transcript.html?ei=5070&en=f79a0ab6dac84413&ex=1179028800&pagewanted=all | title=The Republicans' First Presidential Candidates Debate | newspaper=The New York Times | date=May 3, 2007}}</ref> In 2012, as a candidate for president, the [[Secular Coalition for America]] gave Romney a 100% on accepting evolution.<ref name=":1" />

In October 2011, Romney told the ''[[Las Vegas Sun]]'' that he had not yet taken a serious look at the issue of legalizing online [[poker]], but that he would do so and state a position "[b]efore the caucuses come along".<ref>{{Citation| last = Demirjian| first = Karoun | title = Romney faces tough decision with stance on online gaming| newspaper = [[Las Vegas Sun]] | date = November 24, 2011| url = http://www.lasvegassun.com/news/2011/nov/24/romney-faces-tough-decision-online-gaming/ | access-date = 2011-12-01}}</ref> Just before the Republican caucuses in [[Nevada]], Romney announced his opposition to online gambling, citing the "social costs and people's addictive gambling habits."<ref>{{cite web| last = Collson| first = Brett| title = The Nightly Turbo: Romney Opposes Online Gaming, Florida Denied Casino Bill, and more| publisher = PokerNews| date = February 3, 2012| url = http://www.pokernews.com/news/2012/02/nightly-turbo-romney-opposes-online-gaming-florida-denied-11952.htm| access-date = 2012-02-04}}</ref>

===Guns===

While campaigning to represent Massachusetts in the U.S. Senate in 1994, Romney supported the [[Brady Bill]], which imposed a five-day waiting period on gun sales, and a ban on particular semi-automatic rifles.<ref name="romneynra"/> He said at the time, "That's not going to make me the hero of the NRA. I don't line up with the NRA."<ref name="rvsr"/>
In 2002, during his campaign for the governorship, Romney said: "We do have tough gun laws in Massachusetts; I support them.  I won't chip away at them; I believe they protect us and provide for our safety."<ref name="rvsr">
{{cite news | author = Scot Lehigh | url = https://www.boston.com/news/nation/articles/2007/01/19/romney_vs_romney/ | title = Romney vs. Romney | work = [[The Boston Globe]] | date = January 19, 2007 }}
</ref>

As governor of Massachusetts, in 2004 Romney signed<ref name=mehtaquot>{{cite news|last=Mehta|first=Seema|title=Colorado shooting renews focus on Romney's gun-control stance|url=https://www.latimes.com/politics/la-xpm-2012-jul-22-la-pn-colorado-shooting-renews-focus-on-romneys-gun-control-stance-20120721-story.html|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|date=July 22, 2012}}</ref> a measure permanently extending a statewide ban on [[assault weapon|military-style assault weapons]], such as [[AK-47]]'s and [[Uzi]]'s.<ref name=globeweaponsban>{{cite news|last=Greenberger|first=Scott S.|title=State moves on assault weapons ban|url=https://www.boston.com/news/local/massachusetts/articles/2004/06/24/state_moves_on_assault_weapons_ban/|newspaper=The Boston Globe|date=June 24, 2004}}</ref> At the bill-signing ceremony Romney said, "Deadly assault weapons have no place in Massachusetts. ... These guns are not made for recreation or self-defense. They are instruments of destruction with the sole purpose of hunting down and killing people."<ref name=mehtaquot/> Proponents of the state semi-automatic assault weapons ban had argued that its passage was necessary because a similar ban at the federal level was also expiring.<ref name=globeweaponsban/>

The bill also included several compromise measures sought by gun enthusiasts to lessen restrictions on lawful gun ownership, including an extension of the term of firearms licenses from 4 to 6 years, reinstatement of a 90-day grace period for citizens renewing expired firearms licenses, and establishment of a firearms license review board empowered to consider reinstating ownership status to those who had lost their licenses after having committed certain non-violent misdemeanors more than 5 years in the past.<ref>{{cite news|last=Miner|first=Bradford L.|title=More lenient gun bill goes to Romney|newspaper=Worcester Telegram & Gazette|date=June 25, 2004}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Guerriero Iguerriero|first=Lisa|title=New law eases restrictions on gun owners|newspaper=Sentinel & Enterprise|date=July 6, 2004|location=Fitchburg, MA}}</ref>

In 2005, Governor Romney declared May 7 to be "Right to Bear Arms Day" in Massachusetts,<ref name=weisshifts>{{cite news|last=Weisman|first=Jonathan|title=For Romney, 2005 was key year of policy shifts|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052970204505304577004352121240264|newspaper=The Wall Street Journal|date=November 11, 2011}}</ref> that date having been chosen to coincide with the annual banquet of the Gun Owners' Action League (a Massachusetts gun rights advocacy organization affiliated with the [[National Rifle Association]]).<ref>{{cite web|title=The Romney record: a GOAL special report (February 2007)|url=http://www.goal.org/newspages/romney.html|publisher=Gun Owners' Action League|access-date=August 21, 2012|archive-date=August 25, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120825034158/http://www.goal.org/newspages/romney.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>  Romney's top aides then began meeting almost monthly with members of the Gun Owners' Action League.<ref name=weisshifts/>

In August 2006, just before declaring his candidacy for the 2008 Republican nomination for president, Romney joined the National Rifle Association (NRA) as a lifetime member.<ref name=romneynra>
{{cite news | author = Scott Helman | url = https://www.boston.com/news/local/massachusetts/articles/2007/01/14/romney_retreats_on_gun_control/ | title = Romney, appealing to core GOP voters, toughens pro-gun rhetoric | work = [[The Boston Globe]] | date = January 14, 2007 }}
</ref><ref name=glenjhunt>{{cite news|last=Johnson|first=Glen|title=Romney's hunting experience limited to two trips|url=https://www.chron.com/news/nation-world/article/Romney-s-hunting-experience-limited-to-two-trips-1584135.php|newspaper=The Houston Chronicle|date=April 5, 2007}}</ref><ref name="LeBlanc">
{{cite news | author = Steve LeBlanc | agency = Associated Press | url = https://www.boston.com/news/local/massachusetts/articles/2007/01/14/romney_retreats_on_gun_control/ | title = Romney retreats on gun control: Ex-governor woos Republican votes | work = [[The Boston Globe]] | date = January 14, 2007 }}
</ref> Seeking the endorsement of the NRA, Romney made several statements during the campaign regarding his proficiency with and support for firearms:

<blockquote>I purchased a gun when I was a young man. I've been a hunter pretty much all my life.<ref name=glenjhunt/></blockquote>

<blockquote>Shooting rabbits single shot 22 is pretty hard.<ref>{{YouTube|id=7ug_pt_mQwc|title=NH Voter on Mitt Romney, Varmint Hunter}}</ref></blockquote>

<blockquote>I have a gun of my own. I go hunting myself. I'm a member of the NRA and believe firmly in the right to bear arms. In our state ... there are a series of laws restricting gun ownership in various ways. Over the past four years, I've worked very closely with the Gun Owners' Action League here, which is an affiliate of the NRA, and we've made some changes which I think they feel have been positive steps.<ref name="rvsr"/>
</blockquote>

<blockquote>So I'm a hunter and believe in Second Amendment rights, but I also believe that assault weapons are not needed in the public population.<ref name="thisweekromney">
[https://www.abcnews.go.com/ThisWeek/Politics/story?id=2885156&page=2 Mitt Romney: The Complete Interview] ABC News. Retrieved June 21, 2007
</ref></blockquote>

The Associated Press reported in early 2007 that Romney's "hunting experience is limited to two trips at the bookends of his 60 years: as a 15-year-old, when he hunted rabbits with his cousins on a ranch in Idaho, and last year, when he shot quail on a fenced game preserve in Georgia,"<ref name=glenjhunt/> and that Romney had never sought a hunting license in any of the four states where he had resided. Romney replied by saying that he mainly hunted [[small game]] in Utah, where a license was not required.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/04/07/AR2007040701089.html|title=Four States Report Romney Never Got Hunting Licenses|newspaper=The Washington Post | agency = Associated Press|date=April 8, 2007|access-date=2008-01-08 | first=Glen | last=Johnson}}</ref> He also clarified that he did not 'own' a gun and said that one of his sons keeps two guns at the family vacation home in Utah.<ref name="LeBlanc"/>

In December 2007, still campaigning for the Republican presidential nomination, Romney summed up his general position on gun control at that time as: "we should check on the backgrounds of people who are trying to purchase guns. We also should keep weapons of unusual lethality from being on the street. And finally, we should go after people who use guns in the commission of crimes or illegally, but we should not interfere with the right of law-abiding citizens to own guns either for their own personal protection or hunting or any other lawful purpose."<ref name=MTP12-2007>{{cite news|title=Mitt Romney interview by Tim Russert on Meet The Press|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna22273924|work=NBC News|date=December 17, 2007}}</ref> He also said that, had it come before him as president, he would have signed a renewal of the federal assault weapons ban that had expired.<ref name=MTP12-2007/> The following month, during a presidential primary debate, he noted that the federal assault weapons ban that he would have signed as president had failed in Congress, and he insisted that he would not support any ''new'' gun control legislation: "I do not believe we need new legislation. I do not support any new legislation of an assault weapon ban nature, including that against semiautomatic weapons. I instead believe that we have laws in place that if they're implemented and enforced, will provide the protection and the safety of the American people."<ref>{{cite news|title=2008 Republican Presidential Primary Debate, Boca Raton, Florida (transcript)|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna22799665|newspaper=NBC News|date=January 24, 2008}}</ref>

Romney continued to argue against any new gun control legislation during the 2012 presidential campaign, telling the NRA's national convention that if elected president, he would "enforce current laws, not create new ones that only serve to burden lawful gun owners."<ref>{{cite news|last=Gabriel|first=Trip|title=Mitt Romney assures N.R.A. of support for gun rights|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/04/14/us/politics/mitt-romney-assures-gun-rights-group-of-his-fealty.html|newspaper=The New York Times|date=April 13, 2012}}</ref> [[Gun Owners of America]], which supports gun owners' rights, gave Romney a score of 20% during the 2012 presidential campaign.<ref name=":2">{{cite web|url=https://votesmart.org/candidate/evaluations/21942/mitt-romney#.WzVAadJKiUk|title=Mitt Romney's Ratings and Endorsements|website=votesmart.org}}</ref>

In the wake of a [[2012 Aurora, Colorado shooting|mass shooting at a movie theater in Aurora, Colorado]] in July 2012, Romney maintained in a series of interviews that he opposed any new gun control measures.<ref name=borchguns>{{cite news|last=Borchers|first=Callum|title=Romney says gun laws are adequate|url=http://articles.boston.com/2012-07-26/news/32845722_1_assault-weapons-mitt-romney-gun-laws|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130118175056/http://articles.boston.com/2012-07-26/news/32845722_1_assault-weapons-mitt-romney-gun-laws|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 18, 2013|newspaper=The Boston Globe|date=July 26, 2012}}</ref><ref name=navarroguns>{{cite news|last=Navarro|first=Bruno J.|title=Mitt Romney: New gun laws aren't the answer|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2012/07/23/mitt-romney-new-gun-laws-arent-the-answer.html|archive-url=http://webarchive.loc.gov/all/20120724130851/https://www.cnbc.com/id/48289684/Mitt_Romney_New_Gun_Laws_Aren_t_the_Answer|url-status=live|archive-date=July 24, 2012|publisher=CNBC|date=July 23, 2012}}</ref><ref name=morganguns>{{cite news|title=Mitt Romney interviewed by Piers Morgan (transcript)|url=http://transcripts.cnn.com/TRANSCRIPTS/1207/26/pmt.01.html|publisher=CNN Piers Morgan Tonight|date=July 26, 2012}}</ref> Referring to the alleged perpetrator of the Aurora massacre, Romney said, "This person shouldn't have had any kind of weapons and bombs and other devices, and it was illegal for him to have many of those things already. ... But he had them. And so we can sometimes hope that just changing the law will make all bad things go away. It won't."<ref name="dpaurora">{{cite news|url=http://www.denverpost.com/news/ci_21159342|title=Obama, Romney differ over guns after Colorado attack|last1=Babington|first1=Charles|date=2012-07-25|newspaper=The Denver Post|last2=Pace|first2=Julie}}</ref>

During his Utah Senate campaign in 2018, Romney said that he is open to enhancing background checks on gun purchases and voting for limitations on gun purchases based on age or psychological evaluations.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cnn.com/2018/02/17/politics/romney-gun-measures/index.html|title=Romney open to new gun measures|first=Maeve |last=Reston|work=CNN|access-date=2018-06-19}}</ref> Debating his primary opponent, Mike Kennedy, in Utah, Romney said that he supports a ban on bump stocks which assists a user in bump firing a semi-automatic firearm.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.apnews.com/8c2c0687fdc1465282b7ac0ef9016f82|title=The Latest: Romney debates opponent Mike Kennedy for Senate|work=Associated Press|access-date=2018-06-19|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2022, Romney later became one of ten Republican Senators to support a bipartisan agreement on gun control, which involved a red flag provision, a support for state crisis intervention orders, funding for school safety resources, stronger background checks for buyers under the age of 21, and penalties for straw purchases.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/06/12/politics/senate-gun-safety-agreement/index.html|title=Bipartisan group of senators announces agreement on gun control|publisher=CNN|last1=Bash|first1=Dana|last2=Raju|first2=Manu|last3=Judd|first3=Donald|date=June 12, 2022|access-date=June 12, 2022}}</ref>

===Immigration===
{{see also|Governorship of Mitt Romney#Illegal immigration}}
Romney favors increased [[Immigration to the United States|legal immigration]] to the United States and opposes [[Illegal immigration to the United States|illegal immigration]],<ref>{{cite news| last = Vickers| first = Marcia| author-link = Marcia Vickers| title = The Republicans' Mr. Fix-it| work = Fortune | date = June 27, 2007| url = https://money.cnn.com/magazines/fortune/fortune_archive/2007/07/09/100121803/ | access-date = 2011-11-06}}</ref> but he would respect the work permits to younger illegal immigrants that President Obama had granted.<ref name="dream act"/> In 2006, Romney said he would like to see undocumented immigrants register with the government, pay taxes, and apply for citizenship, but that they should not be given any priority or special treatment over immigrants who have applied for citizenship legally.<ref>
{{cite news | url=https://www.boston.com/news/local/massachusetts/articles/2006/03/29/romney_declines_to_take_stand_on_senate_immigration_bill/ |title=Romney declines to take stand on Senate immigration bill | last=Miga | first=Andrew | work=[[The Boston Globe]] | date=March 29, 2006 | access-date=2008-01-27}}
</ref> During the 2008 presidential primary campaign, he embraced the support of Arizona's Maricopa County Sheriff [[Joe Arpaio]], known for his very tough stance on immigration. Arpaio served as honorary chair of Romney's Arizona campaign organization<ref>{{cite news|last=Bonisteel|first=Sara|title=Arizona Sheriff Joe Arpaio tells FOX News why Mitt Romney Picked him for presidential campaign|url=https://www.foxnews.com/story/arizona-sheriff-joe-arpaio-tells-fox-news-why-mitt-romney-picked-him-for-presidential-campaign|newspaper=Fox News|date=February 28, 2007}}</ref> and as a campaign surrogate for Romney on immigration.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kaczynski|first=Andrew|title=Joe Arpaio was Romney Arizona campaign chair in 2008|url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/andrewkaczynski/flashback-joe-arpaio-was-romney-arizona-campaign|publisher=BuzzFeed|date=March 1, 2012|access-date=September 28, 2012}}</ref>

During the 2012 presidential election primary campaign, Romney called Arizona's approach to illegal immigration "a model for the nation."<ref name=memoliaz>{{cite news|last=Memoli|first=Michael A.|title=Romney calls Arizona immigration law a model for the nation|url=https://www.latimes.com/politics/la-xpm-2012-feb-22-la-pn-gop-debate-illegal-immigration-20120222-story.html|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|date=February 22, 2012}}</ref> He vowed that on his first day in office as president, he would bring an end to the lawsuits the Obama Administration's Justice Department had brought challenging Arizona's immigration policy.<ref name=memoliaz/> He also praised the anti-illegal immigration efforts of Kansas Secretary of State [[Kris Kobach]], a law professor who had drafted much of [[Arizona SB 1070|Arizona's SB 1070 immigration enforcement law]] and similar measures around the country. Campaigning with Kobach in January 2012, Romney said, "We need more conservative leaders like Kris willing to stand up for the rule of law. With Kris on the team, I look forward to working with him to take forceful steps to curtail illegal immigration and to support states like South Carolina and Arizona that are stepping forward to address this problem."<ref>{{cite news|last=Fabian|first=Jordan|title=Romney's endorsers cut both ways on immigration|url=http://univisionnews.tumblr.com/post/15967713499/romneys-endorsers-cut-both-ways-on-immigration|archive-url=https://archive.today/20121225134737/http://univisionnews.tumblr.com/post/15967713499/romneys-endorsers-cut-both-ways-on-immigration|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 25, 2012|newspaper=Univision Noticias|date=January 16, 2012}}</ref> When the Supreme Court struck down parts of Arizona's SB 1070 in June 2012, a Romney campaign spokesman said that Romney supports the rights of states to make their own immigration laws when the federal government has failed to address illegal immigration.<ref>{{cite news|last=Burns|first=Alexander|title=The Romney camp's line on Arizona|url=https://www.politico.com/blogs/burns-haberman/2012/06/the-romney-camps-line-on-arizona-updated-127229|newspaper=Politico|date=June 25, 2012}}</ref>

To help combat illegal immigration across the border with Mexico, Romney has said that the U.S. must erect a fence along the entire 2,600 mile border, equipped with technology to detect attempts to breach the barrier, and outfitted with adequate numbers of border patrol agents.<ref name=simivimi>{{cite news|title=The Republican Debate at the Reagan Library (Simi Valley, CA)|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/09/08/us/politics/08republican-debate-text.html?pagewanted=all|newspaper=The New York Times|date=September 7, 2011}}</ref> Romney's positions were given mixed reactions and ratings by anti-immigration groups. [[NumbersUSA|Numbers USA]] gave him a D grade for his positions in 2011 and a 64% score in his 2012 campaign.<ref name=":2" /> [[ProEnglish]], which seeks to make English the official language of the United States, gave Romney an overall 73% grade.<ref name=":2" />

Romney also said during the primary campaign that he would seek to make the U.S. a much less hospitable place for undocumented immigrants by eliminating what he called the magnets that attract them.<ref name=simivimi/><ref name=foximi>{{cite news|title=Fox News-Google GOP debate|url=http://www.foxnews.com/politics/2011/09/22/fox-news-google-gop-2012-presidential-debate/|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130123092201/http://www.foxnews.com/politics/2011/09/22/fox-news-google-gop-2012-presidential-debate/|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 23, 2013|newspaper=Fox News|date=September 22, 2011}}</ref> An example of a magnet, he said, would be offering to undocumented immigrants the same tuition discounts that are offered to legal residents who attend public colleges in their states, a benefit that rival candidate Governor [[Rick Perry]] supported for Texas students who had been brought as children to the U.S. by their undocumented immigrant parents.<ref name=foximi/> Romney similarly said that he opposed all forms of amnesty because he regards amnesty as another magnet for illegal immigration.<ref name=cnnimiwdc>{{cite news|title=CNN National security presidential primary debate (Washington, DC)|url=http://archives.cnn.com/TRANSCRIPTS/1111/22/se.06.html|newspaper=CNN|date=November 22, 2011|access-date=September 29, 2012|archive-date=June 23, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120623120320/http://archives.cnn.com/TRANSCRIPTS/1111/22/se.06.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He vowed that as president he would veto the [[DREAM Act]] (legislation which would allow individuals who had been brought to the U.S. as children when their families immigrated illegally an opportunity to qualify for permanent residency if they met certain qualifications), because he considered it yet another magnet for illegal immigration.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://abcnews.go.com/blogs/politics/2011/12/mitt-romney-vows-to-veto-dream-act-if-president/ |title=Mitt Romney Vows to Veto Dream Act if President |work=ABC News |date=2011-12-31 |access-date=2012-04-12}}</ref><ref name=nytdreamact>{{cite news|last=Weisman|first=Jonathan|title=Rubio, in appeal to G.O.P.'s conscience, urges compromise on Dream act|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/04/20/us/politics/marco-rubio-urges-republicans-to-pass-dream-act.html|newspaper=The New York Times|date=April 19, 2012}}</ref>

Romney has argued that a key step to reducing illegal immigration would be to reduce the job opportunities available for undocumented immigrants. He has said that requiring employers to confirm each worker's immigration status using an [[E-Verify]]-type database, such as in Arizona, and punishing employers who hire workers lacking proper documentation, would lead employers to stop hiring undocumented immigrants, with the result that fewer immigrants would choose to come to the U.S. illegally, and many of those who are already in the U.S. would "[[self-deportation|self-deport]]."<ref>{{cite news|title=Romney says he favors 'self-deportation'|url=http://articles.nydailynews.com/2012-01-24/news/30657385_1_mitt-romney-illegal-immigrants-deportation|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120312022656/http://articles.nydailynews.com/2012-01-24/news/30657385_1_mitt-romney-illegal-immigrants-deportation|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 12, 2012|newspaper=New York Daily News|access-date=29 May 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Romney's "self deportation" plan draws laughs|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/video/watch/?id=7396174n|work=CBS News|access-date=29 May 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Romney's Plan for 'Self-Deportation' Has Conservative Support|url=http://thecaucus.blogs.nytimes.com/2012/01/24/romneys-plan-for-self-deportation-has-conservative-support/|newspaper=NY Times|access-date=29 May 2012|first=Julia|last=Preston|date=January 24, 2012}}</ref>

In June 2012, President Obama issued an executive order instructing officers of the federal government to defer deporting young undocumented immigrants who had been brought to the U.S. as children and who met certain requirements, such as serving in the military or being successful students.<ref>{{cite news|last=Cohen|first=Tom|title=Obama administration to stop deporting some young illegal immigrants|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2012/06/15/politics/immigration/index.html|work=CNN|date=June 16, 2012}}</ref> The executive order was intended to temporarily implement parts of the DREAM Act until a permanent fix could being agreed upon by Congress and the White House. When Romney was asked his opinion of the president's executive order, he responded by saying that he would reveal his own long-term policy on the subject at a later date.<ref>{{cite news|last=Downes|first=Lawrence|title=Mitt Romney's secret plan|url=http://takingnote.blogs.nytimes.com/2012/09/20/mitt-romneys-secret-plan/|newspaper=The New York Times (editorial page blog)|date=September 20, 2012}}</ref><ref>Avlon, John. [http://www.thedailybeast.com/articles/2012/06/22/policy-black-hole-mitt-romney-keeps-his-ideas-to-himself.html "Policy Black Hole: Mitt Romney Keeps His Ideas To Himself."] ''The Daily Beast'', 22 June 2012.</ref> Romney later said that he would respect the [[Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals|work permits that Obama had granted]].<ref name="dream act">Grant, David. [http://www.csmonitor.com/USA/Elections/President/2012/1002/Critics-pounce-after-Mitt-Romney-says-he-d-honor-Obama-approvals-for-illegals "Critics pounce after Mitt Romney says he'd honor Obama approvals for illegals."] ''CSM'', 2 October 2012.</ref>

In terms of promoting more legal immigration, Romney has proposed loosening immigration rules to increase the entry of highly skilled immigrants into the U.S., allowing more high-skill visas to be granted and raising the quotas of high-skilled immigrants allowed from certain countries. Romney has noted that high-skilled immigrants are more likely to start companies and create jobs than other immigrants. He has said the U.S. should grant permanent residency to "every foreign student who obtains an advanced degree in math, science, or engineering at a U.S. university." He has also proposed streamlining the temporary worker visa issuance system so that temporary agricultural and tourism workers could be processed more efficiently.
